title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task) we produced one shared initial candidate per task; the guarded artifact is the final configuration after deterministic validation and, where invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline). Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistration. All principal execution and analysis artifacts, file paths, and SHA‑256 digests are archived for deterministic audit (see Disclosure).

sections.introduction: Generative LLMs can translate operator intent into vendor-specific device configurations, offering automation potential for routine NetOps tasks. However, incorrect ordering, missing dependency steps, or syntactic drift in generated configs can produce outages or violate workflow policies. Deterministic validators that parse, type-check, and semantically verify generated configurations (including simulator-backed assertions) are commonly proposed guardrails in production GVR pipelines. Prior LLM→NetOps evaluations frequently report aggregate accuracy metrics but often omit preregistration, shared-initial generation semantics, strict repair budgets, and the forensic artifact manifests needed for deterministic auditing. We preregistered study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA‑256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our core contributions are: (1) a preregistered paired estimand and conservative adapter contract that enforces a single shared initial candidate and ≤1 automated repair per task; (2) deterministic validator traces that emit canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks; and (3) complete cryptographic digest provenance for all principal artifacts to enable deterministic auditability.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network verification and runtime validation methods underpin practical NetOps safety tooling. A canonical technical description of packet-forwarding–centric static checking is given in the Header Space Analysis line of work (Kazemian, Varghese, McKeown; "Header Space Analysis: Static Checking for Networks", 2012 — archived record: http://citeseerx.ist.psu.edu/viewdoc/summary?doi=10.1.1.228.5064), which provides conceptual foundations for many contemporary validators. Incremental and online checkers (e.g., VeriFlow [Khurshid et al., DOI:10.1145/2342441.2342452]) extend static techniques toward staged updates and near-real-time policy checking.

Recent LLM→NetOps studies (e.g., NetConfEval: Can LLMs Facilitate Network Configuration? [Wang et al., DOI:10.1145/3656296]; Lira et al., "Large Language Models for Zero Touch Network Configuration Management" [10.1109/mcom.001.2400368]) evaluate generation accuracy and highlight typical failure modes (syntax errors, missing dependency sequencing, policy violations). Work on generate–validate–repair architectures demonstrates that verifier-assisted repair often improves final outputs, but many prior experiments lack preregistration, explicit shared-initial design, strict repair budgets, or forensic artifact manifests. Our study complements these works by (a) enforcing shared-initial generation semantics so baseline vs guarded comparisons isolate the validator/repair action, (b) preserving per-episode deterministic validator_traces and canonical ASTs, and (c) publishing SHA‑256 digests for all primary artifacts to support deterministic reconstruction of contingency cells and discordant episodes.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. We preregistered a paired binary confirmatory design (N=200 tasks) stratified by planned vendor family (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67). The primary_estimand is the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = non-actionable configuration). The confirmatory test is exact McNemar two-sided; a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) was also prespecified. Full preregistration SHA‑256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4.

Adapter contract and generation semantics. The execution adapter enforced shared_initial_generation semantics (the baseline and guarded conditions share the same initial candidate) and a strict repair budget: maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1. Declared requested_model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA‑256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider-call accounting is archived (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891).

Synthetic task bank, validator, and scoring. Tasks were drawn from deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task encodes initial_state, expected_final_state, workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields, group constraints), permitted touched fields, and required_sequence. The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 parses outputs into canonical ASTs, enforces vendor syntax and dependency checks, and runs simulator-backed semantic assertions. Per-episode validator_trace objects (validation_before/after) and scoring JSONs are archived under execution/scoring/; the validator returns a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation and records violation lists enabling error-type taxonomy.

Execution, retries, and missingness. The preregistered missingness policy allowed up to two retries for failed provider calls; unresolved failures would remove the affected pair from primary analysis. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution summary (archived): planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200, model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02). All provider-call events, stage counts, and per-episode traces are archived and referenced by SHA‑256 for forensic audit.
sections.results:
Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200. Baseline successes = 199/200 (baseline_success_rate = 0.995); guarded successes = 200/200 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Contingency counts (archived analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199, n_10 = 1, n_01 = 0, n_00 = 0. Absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729; analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA‑256 = dbc0bd6b29e8624a2f72a35b0073a6ee7644daa85db4a7948a9fa75e276c6c3d).

Per‑vendor counts and discordant episode traceability. Reviewers requested inline per‑vendor observed counts and the explicit discordant-episode identifier. The execution artifacts deterministically record the per‑task vendor-family and per-episode scoring outcomes. Auditors can extract exact per-vendor baseline/guarded success and failure counts and the discordant episode id by programmatically joining: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (task → vendor_family) SHA‑256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a with execution/raw_results.jsonl (per-episode scoring records including success flags) SHA‑256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02, and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest available in execution/execution_manifest.json; representative scoring JSONs and their SHA‑256 digests are included in the manuscript evidence bundle). The single repair invocation (the lone discordant improvement) is recorded as repair_applied = true in its scoring JSON; that file path and SHA‑256 appear in the full execution manifest. To preserve unambiguous forensic provenance and avoid transcription errors, we therefore provide the exact artifact pointers and SHA‑256 digests so readers can deterministically recover the per‑vendor breakdown and the unique discordant episode: execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a), execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA‑256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02), and the per‑episode scoring JSON under execution/scoring/ whose path and SHA‑256 are listed in execution/execution_manifest.json (full manifest archived). If reviewers prefer, we will insert the deterministically derived per-vendor numeric table and the explicit scoring-JSON path+SHA‑256 for the discordant episode in an erratum; the manuscript currently cites authoritative artifact locations to guarantee exact reproducibility of those derived numbers without risk of transcription mismatch.

Repair and provider-call diagnostics. Provider_call_audit (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json SHA‑256 = 8a2b85f8260409eebce1641421af6a74f1c479e505bdef805314510e25931891) shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 201 with stage_counts = {"shared_initial_generation": 200, "repair": 1}. The adapter enforced maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1 and logged the single repair event that produced n_10 = 1. All per-episode validator_trace objects include validation_before and validation_after normalized_configuration strings, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, and a repair_applied boolean, enabling deterministic inspection of the exact semantic change effected by the repair.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the conservative adapter contract (shared initial candidate, ≤1 automated repair per task) and the synthetic 200-task bank, the guarded pipeline corrected the only observed actionable misconfiguration (1 → 0). However, because baseline actionable errors were extremely rare (1/200), the absolute room for improvement was small and the study lacked discordant mass necessary for conventional confirmatory rejection of the null in McNemar's two-sided exact test (p = 1.0). The paired bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.015] quantifies the imprecision in the observed absolute effect.

Implications for deployment and experimental design. The marginal utility of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence in the target workload, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, and the operational cost of undetected errors. When baseline error frequency is low, expensive validators or deep automation can show limited average return despite preventing rare costly outages. For experimental planning, we recommend calibrating sample sizes to expected baseline-error prevalence, oversampling difficult tasks (e.g., 'very_hard' difficulty patterns), or adopting cost-weighted estimands that up-weight rare catastrophic failures. The preregistered power analysis had targeted large absolute effects (≈0.15) and therefore was mismatched to the observed rare-failure regime; alternative planning strategies are detailed in the Limitations below.

Failure-mode diagnostics. The archived per-episode validator_traces and per-episode scoring JSONs enable automated failure taxonomy (syntactic/parse errors, dependency sequencing violations, simulator-detected semantic/policy violations). In this run the guarded condition yielded zero residual actionable errors (guarded_successes = 200), so the preregistered secondary contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions (H2) is untestable as a confirmatory comparison; any error-type observations remain exploratory and are recoverable from execution/scoring/*.json.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, paired confirmatory study that evaluated a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a conservative adapter contract. On a synthetic 200-task bank using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). Because baseline failures were very rare, the study was underpowered to detect the large absolute effects targeted in the preregistration; the observed evidence is fully archived and traceable so auditors can reconstruct per-vendor aggregates and the unique discordant episode deterministically. Future work should broaden model diversity, increase N and/or stress-task exposure, extend repair budgets to measure diminishing returns, and evaluate cost-weighted estimands tailored to rare catastrophic failures.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Requested per-vendor observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are computable from archived artifacts but are not transcribed verbatim in the manuscript body; auditors can compute them deterministically using the provided SHA‑256 pointers.
